title: Race to semis: Qualification scenarios at T20WC 2026
byline: With three rounds of matches completed for each team at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, the race for the semi-finals is heating up.

title: Garbage piles near health ministry raise dengue concerns
byline: Garbage has accumulated along Norris Canal Road and several surrounding areas within a 50-metre radius of the Ministry of Health, creating potential dengue mosquito breeding grounds, according to Specialist Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa, Chairman of the Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance for Medical and Civil Rights.

title: Rs. 210Bn money trail: Mastermind detained, hunt on for accomplices
byline: The alleged mastermind behind a large-scale money laundering operation accused of illegally transferring more than Rs. 210 billion (over US$700 million) out of Sri Lanka under the guise of importing goods has been detained by the Financial Investigation Division, with further investigations now underway.

title: Japan quintuples foreigner visa fees in first price hike since 1978
byline: Japan has implemented a fivefold increase to visa fees for foreigners, marking the first price hike in nearly 50 years.

title: First high-level US-Iran talks see key agreements after brief walkout
byline: The United States and Iran reached several key understandings during their first high-level talks in Switzerland, agreeing on a 60-day timeline to finalise a deal, setting up a High Level Committee to oversee the negotiations, and establishing communication mechanisms for the Strait of Hormuz, despite a tense start and a brief walkout by Iranian negotiators.

title: Twins conjoined at head separated after 40 hours of AI-assisted surgery
byline: Twin sisters who spent the first 19 months of their lives joined at the skull were successfully separated in a stunning string of AI-assisted surgeries — and are now happy and thriving toddlers turning three.

title: Hold SLC elections or get blacklisted, ICC informs President AKD
byline: The International Cricket Council has put forward a request to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to hold the elections of Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) on or before July 31, and has emphasised that if local authorities fail to do so, Sri Lanka once again risks being blacklisted by the ICC, the Daily Mirror reliably learns.

title: Colombo Port transhipment growth accelerates as CWIT ramps up operations
byline: The Port of Colombo recorded significant growth in container transhipment volumes in April 2026, building upon its record-breaking performance in the previous year.

title: Sri Lanka, Thailand urge stronger business ties to overcome ‘unfamiliarity’ to boost trade and investments
byline: Sri Lanka and Thailand are pushing for deeper economic integration, with officials from both nations urging their respective private sectors to bridge the gap of unfamiliarity to build trust and unlock the full potential of bilateral trade and investments.

title: IMF team to visit Sri Lanka this week
byline: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) country team is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka from June 24 to 30 for a formal staff visit to review the nation’s ongoing economic reform programme and assess the implementation of critical structural reforms.

title: France bans alcohol at music festival events under red heatwave alert
byline: France has banned alcohol at some events at a massive national music festival on Sunday as a heatwave pushes temperatures towards record levels.

title: Alleged mastermind behind Rs. 210 Billion illegal Dollar transfer network arrested
byline: The Financial Investigation Division has arrested the alleged mastermind behind a large-scale money laundering operation accused of illegally transferring more than Rs. 210 billion (over US$700 million) out of Sri Lanka under the guise of importing goods.

title: Explosion at Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG facility injures 54, leaves 18 missing
byline: An explosion at Qatar’s main liquefied natural gas processing facility has injured 54 people and left 18 others missing, authorities have said.

title: Beware of fake PHIs extorting money
byline: The Sri Lanka Public Health Inspectors’ Union has warned the public to be alert to individuals impersonating Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) and extorting money from households and institutions under the guise of official duties.

title: Sri Lanka Army calls for applications for Officer Cadet Courses
byline: The Sri Lanka Army has invited applications for vacancies in the Officer Cadets Short Course (Diploma) and the Lady Officer Cadets Course (Diploma) in the Regular Force.

title: Indian expat dies while playing badminton in Dubai
byline: A 42-year-old Indian expatriate from Kerala died after collapsing while playing shuttle badminton in Dubai, according to a report by Manorama Online.

title: Over 1,000 Dengue cases logged in 24 hours
byline: Sri Lanka recorded 1,069 dengue cases in the past 24 hours, Acting Director of the National Dengue Control Unit, Dr. Kapila Kannangara said.

title: Businesses earning over Rs. 100,000 daily must register for VAT and SSCL from July 1st
byline: Nuwara Eliya District Senior Deputy Commissioner of Inland Revenue E.D. Karunaratne said that all service providers and businesses with a daily income exceeding Rs. 100,000 must register for Value Added Tax (VAT) and the Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL) from July 1st.

title: Assistant Secretary of State Paul Kapur arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs S. Paul Kapur arrived in Colombo on a three-day visit from June 21 to June 24.

title: Global Sri Lankan Forum urges President to intervene over Suresh Sallay’s health and legal rights
byline: The Global Sri Lankan Forum (GSLF) has called on the President to urgently intervene on humanitarian grounds regarding the rapidly deteriorating health condition of the former Director of the State Intelligence Service (SIS), Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay.

title: School Principal arrested over sex abuse
byline: The principal of a school in Koslanda in Bandarawela who had been arrested on suspicion of sexually abusing a ten year old schoolgirl was produced before Bandarawela Magistrate Gemunu Chandrasekara and remanded till July 10,’’The 56 year old suspect was a father of two children.

title: Safeguard existing apparel factories before producing fabrics from banana tree bark: Sajith
byline: The government should focus on safeguarding the existing apparel factories first rather than focusing on producing fabrics from banana tree barks, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa said today.

title: Russian State-Owned Companies Cleared to Bid for Sri Lanka Fuel Tenders
byline: In a bid to improve competitiveness in fuel purchasing from the global market, the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has registered two Russian state owned companies allowing them to participate in the tender process, an official said yesterday.

title: CID probe sought over substandard medical equipment supplied to hospitals
byline: A complaint has been lodged with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) calling for a comprehensive investigation into the supply and use of substandard medical equipment in government hospitals, amid the withdrawal of cardiac stents, angiogram catheters and colostomy bags.

title: MSD recalls hospitals to withdraw colostomy bags, catheters from hospitals immediately
byline: The Medical Supplies Division (MSD) has ordered the immediate withdrawal of several batches of two medical devices supplied to government hospitals — a colostomy appliance and an angiographic catheter — following reports of defects and performance issues that could affect patient safety and treatment outcomes.

title: One dead, 10 injured in multi-vehicle crash in Kegalle
byline: A woman was killed and ten others were injured following a multi-vehicle accident in the Mangalagama area of Molagoda, Kegalle today (June 22).

title: Emotional Chamari takes blame for Sri Lanka loss at T20WC
byline: Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu believes she has let her side down and missed what could be her final chance to guide them to the knockout stages of the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup.

title: Delft, Nainativu and Analaitivu set for round-the-clock power
byline: Residents of Nainativu (Nagadeepa), Analaitivu and Delft islands will soon benefit from a 24-hour uninterrupted electricity supply through a new hybrid renewable energy system currently under construction, Energy Minister Anura Karunatilaka said during an inspection tour of the project.

title: PMD responds to Daily Mirror article on Sri Lanka Cricket
byline: The President’s Media Division (PMD) has issued a statement in response to today’s Daily Mirror article titled “Hold SLC Elections or Get Blacklisted, ICC Informs President AKD.”

title: UK’s Starmer resigns as prime minister
byline: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has resigned in a televised statement after coming under mounting pressure from his own Labour Party.

title: Rupee edges lower against US Dollar
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee recorded a marginal depreciation against the US Dollar today (22), compared to last Friday, with the selling rate rising to Rs. 339.

title: Sri Lanka reaffirms neutral foreign policy in talks with senior US Official
byline: Foreign Affairs Minister Vijitha Herath has reaffirmed Sri Lanka’s commitment to maintaining neutrality and adhering strictly to international law during discussions with Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs S. Paul Kapur.

title: Oil falls after US-Iran talks conclude in Switzerland
byline: Oil prices declined on Monday after U.S.-Iran talks concluded in ​Switzerland with Tehran saying it had secured waivers for oil and petrochemical exports, easing worries about a supply shortage ‌in global markets.

title: Explosion at Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG facility injures 54, leaves 18 missing
byline: An explosion at Qatar’s main liquefied natural gas processing facility has injured 54 people and left 18 others missing, authorities have said.

title: Emotional Chamari takes blame for Sri Lanka loss at T20WC
byline: A sad Chamari Athapaththu reflects on Sri Lanka’s loss to the West Indies that leaves the side with only a slim chance of reaching the semi-finals of the T20 World Cup.

title: US provides Rs. 1.2 Billion satellite communications system to Sri Lanka Navy
byline: The United States today announced the provision of a Fleet Broadband satellite communications system worth approximately US$4 million (over Rs. 1.2 billion) to the Sri Lanka Navy, in a move aimed at strengthening maritime security and connectivity across the Indian Ocean.

title: Ex-Wimbledon champion Vondrousova given four-year ban
byline: Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has been banned for four years for refusing an anti-doping test last year.

title: Qatar says gas export terminal blast killed 13 as workers tried to resume operations
byline: An explosion tore through Qatar’s key natural gas export terminal Sunday night as workers tried to resume operations after Iran bombed it during the war , causing a fire that killed at least 13 people and hurt dozens more.

title: Three dead in Philippines high school shooting over bullying ’grudge’
byline: Three students have been killed and more injured after two of their peers opened fire at a high school in central Philippines, police say.

title: SC to hear appeal on Minister Wijepala’s parliamentary eligibility
byline: The Supreme Court today granted special leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that dismissed a challenge to the parliamentary eligibility of Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala.

title: Pushpika de Silva crown removal case: Verdict scheduled for October 17
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today fixed October 17 to deliver judgment in the case concerning the alleged forcible removal of the crown from Pushpika de Silva, the winner of the Mrs. Sri Lanka 2021 pageant, causing her injuries.

title: WhatsApp to be led by Indian start-up founder as Will Cathcart steps back
byline: WhatsApp boss Will Cathcart has announced that he is leaving his role.

title: US Assistant Secretary of State meets President Dissanayake
byline: United States Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Dr. Paul Kapur met President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat during his visit to Sri Lanka.

title: US Treasury eases sanctions, issues 60-day license for Iranian oil amid progress in peace talks
byline: In a major shift in Middle Eastern energy and security dynamics, the US Department of the Treasury on Monday issued a temporary 60-day general license authorising transactions related to the production, delivery, and sale of Iranian crude oil, petrochemicals, and petroleum products.

title: Qatar says gas export terminal blast killed 13 as workers tried to resume operations
byline: An explosion tore through Qatar’s key natural gas export terminal Sunday night as workers tried to resume operations after Iran bombed it during the war , causing a fire that killed at least 13 people and hurt dozens more.

title: Pushpika de Silva crown removal case: Verdict scheduled for September 14
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today fixed September 14 to deliver judgment in the case concerning the alleged forcible removal of the crown from Pushpika de Silva, the winner of the Mrs. Sri Lanka 2021 pageant, causing her injuries.
